page: Microsoft Azure E48pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. It features 48 dedicated physical cores with single-thread execution and is equipped with 384 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The server includes 2835 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier memory performance, with uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidths ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. This high memory throughput is reflected in a top-tier Passmark memory score and exceptional database operation performance. Multi-core processing is strong, as evidenced by top 10% Geekbench multi-core scores and top 25% stress-ng multi-core CPU results. However, single-core performance is average, and large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with prompt processing on a 70B model ranking in the bottom 25%.

The E48pds_v6 offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads due to its ARM architecture, which provides a favorable performance-per-resource profile. Given the combination of 384 GB of RAM, fast memory bandwidth, and substantial local storage, this server is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, and large-scale data processing tasks. It is less optimal for workloads requiring high single-threaded performance or heavy vector instruction sets, as AVX and AMX extensions are absent.
